claims.text: The cancellation fee is conjunctive: POL-NS-01 makes it chargeable ONLY IF all four of its conditions hold, and the party asserting the charge carries each of them, so the rider wins by breaking any single limb. The limb that decides this case is (c) - a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the free waiting period in force. For this trip that period is 180 seconds: trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec is 180 and platform_policy.no_show_threshold_sec is null, and under fee_schedule.resolution_rule the platform_policy figure governs because the record carries one. Limb (c) measures that dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the driver's arrival tap - which is precisely the margin on which this fee lives or dies.

On the platform's own instruments the free waiting period the rider is said to have failed to attend had not been served when the driver cancelled. The wait_timer_started event in trip_record records the 180-second free waiting period beginning at 18:35:51 ('Free waiting period of 180 s started'), and the trip was terminated at 18:38:50 - 179 seconds later - with no wait_timer_expired event anywhere in the record. POL-NS-06 makes the cancellation fee unchargeable and refunds it in full where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force under POL-NS-01(c), and that is what the platform's own wait clock shows here.

The dwell can only be the single qualifying in-geofence run, because the traffic advisory that POL-NS-06(i) requires before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed is absent from this bundle. EV-ADVIS-02742-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no payload and has admissibility weight 0.0 - I disclose that impairment expressly - so limb (i) is unavailable and no time the driver spent outside the arrival radius can be recovered into the clock. Stripping out everything limb (i) cannot supply, the effective dwell is the single 181-second run at derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run: a margin of exactly one second over the 180-second minimum on the GPS clock, and a one-second shortfall on the platform's wait-timer clock. A fee that survives only inside a one-second margin on one clock and fails on the other should not be taken from the rider.

The chargeability of this fee is measured by the driver's arrival and dwell, not by where the rider's device happened to be: POL-NS-06 refunds the fee 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. The rider track in this bundle holds 46 fixes but no qualifying fix inside the 100 m rider presence radius, and the chat_log holds no rider message, so POL-NS-04 cannot be run on this record - and that is all it means. The rider's track neither establishes the fee nor defeats it, and the dispute has to be decided on the driver's own evidence.

The driver terminated this trip at the first second the minimum dwell became available - 18:38:50 against a 180-second period running from the first qualifying fix at 18:35:49 - and the only message in the chat_log is the driver's own 'im at the pickup point' sent 20 seconds after the arrival tap and never followed up. A cancellation timed to the second of the fee's availability is the pattern POL-NS-07's anti-farming guard exists to police; the guard does not bite on this record, driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d being 0 against completed_trips_30d of 131, so nothing in POL-NS-07 requires the one-second dwell margin to be read generously - and it should not be.

claims.text: The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event for this trip: the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 18:35:49, some six minutes after being assigned at 18:29:40. Limb (a) of the baseline no-show test is therefore satisfied on the face of the trip record, and the rider's assertion that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is contradicted by the record — nine minutes and ten seconds separate the request from the cancellation.

The GPS trace places the driver inside the arrival geofence, not merely near it. The trace yields 19 qualifying in-radius fixes and the driver's qualifying run begins at the arrival timestamp 18:35:49 and ends only at the cancellation at 18:38:50. The applicable arrival radius is 50 m for the STANDARD zone class recorded on this trip, as POL-NS-02 sets it and as the arrival thresholds block restates it.

The driver held position continuously inside the geofence for 181 seconds, from the first qualifying fix at 18:35:49 to the cancellation at 18:38:50. That meets and exceeds the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec as POL-NS-01(c) directs. The trace's own shortfall figure is minus one second — a one-second surplus, not a shortfall — so the waiting-period-shortfall route under POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to operate on.

The trip was terminated by the driver at 18:38:50 under cancellation reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, and that timestamp falls after the required 180-second dwell had elapsed (18:35:49 plus 180 seconds is 18:38:49). Limb (d) holds on the record.

POL-NS-05's false-arrival route is not engaged. The arrival marker timestamp 18:35:49 coincides exactly with the first qualifying in-geofence fix from which the waiting clock runs — dwell_start_offset_sec is 0.0 — so there is no early tap and no corrected clock for POL-NS-05 to compute. The platform's own wait timer started one second later at 18:35:51 and ran to the cancellation.

POL-NS-03's wrong-entrance route is not engaged either. That clause governs only where the driver's stationary fixes lie outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's qualifying fixes lie inside the 50 m radius itself, so the driver arrived at the pickup point and the 400 m wrong-face test never opens.

The rider cannot be exonerated under POL-NS-04. Limb (a) fails because the only message in the chat log is the driver's — 'im at the pickup point', sent 18:36:09 and read at 18:36:39 — and the rider posted nothing during the waiting window. Limb (c) affirmatively fails as well: every one of the rider's 46 recorded fixes sits between 622 m and 630 m from the pickup pin, far outside the 100 m Standard-class rider presence radius, giving zero qualifying rider fixes across the window. POL-NS-04 has no foothold.

No traffic advisory covers the pickup road. EV-ADVIS-02742-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-NS-06(i)'s accumulation of separate in-geofence intervals is unavailable and nothing can reduce the required minimum dwell. I disclose that impairment expressly under POL-GEN-02. It makes no difference to this case because the driver's dwell is a single unbroken in-geofence run that already satisfies the minimum on its own.

The fare ledger raises no integrity defect for the rider to exploit: the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line is 4.50 SGD, which is exactly the figure platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd states for this trip, so the line reconciles with the resolution rule and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. Payment status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00.

POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the 4.50 SGD cancellation fee in force, that is 3.60 SGD. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, which is not '4 or more', so neither limb of that test is met and compensation is payable rather than withheld. The outcome this trip produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, not a bare refusal to refund.

ruling.explanation: This dispute is over the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee shown on the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02742), and it turns on whether all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold. They do. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:35:49. (b) The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02742) places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 18:35:49, and it holds 19 qualifying in-radius fixes, so the arrival test of POL-NS-02 is met; the arrival marker's own timestamp coincides with that fix, so POL-NS-05 finds no false marker to correct. (c) The continuous in-geofence dwell runs from that first qualifying fix at 18:35:49 to the cancellation at 18:38:50, i.e. 181 seconds against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). POL-NS-01(c) expressly measures the dwell from the first qualifying GPS fix and not from the 'arrived' event or the platform wait timer, so the submission that the wait-timer start at 18:35:51 leaves a 179-second shortfall is declined: the wrong clock was used. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 18:38:50 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) recognises, at or after the moment the dwell elapsed. The rider's other routes do not open. POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to operate on, because the effective in-geofence dwell (181 s) exceeds the minimum; POL-NS-03 does not apply, because the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m radius, not in the 50-400 m wrong-entrance band; POL-NS-04 does not exonerate, because the only chat message is the driver's own, sent 18:36:09, and the rider's 46 fixes sit 622-630 m from the pin, outside the 100 m rider-presence radius. The traffic advisory that POL-NS-06(i) requires before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed is MISSING (EV-ADVIS-02742-01, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, disclosed by both sides), so no outside-radius time can be recovered - which changes nothing here, because the driver's dwell is a single unbroken in-geofence run. The fee therefore stands, and POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of SGD 4.50, which is SGD 3.60. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, below the threshold of 4, so compensation is payable rather than withheld. Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and amount_sgd mirrors driver_compensation_sgd; the rider's charge itself is left as it stands and is not a second payment. Confidence is capped at 1.0, the weight of the GPS trace and trip record that carry the deciding facts. No clause produces a referral: the arrival marker was not false under POL-NS-05(ii), the RIDER_NO_SHOW code was correctly selected, and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is met (the two-second difference between the wait-timer start and the GPS dwell start is well inside POL-NS-08(a), and POL-NS-01(c) resolves which clock governs). The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so this provisional ruling executes automatically, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

Both parties: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee stands, and the driver is to be paid SGD 3.60 as compensation. Per POL-GEN-03, on a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling amount_sgd carries the same figure as driver_compensation_sgd; it is the money this ruling moves, not a refund to the rider.

POL-NS-01 requires all four of its conditions and each one holds on this record. (a) EV-TRIP-02742 carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 18:35:49. (b) EV-GPS-02742 places the driver inside the STANDARD-zone 50 m arrival radius from 18:35:49 onward — 19 qualifying in-radius fixes at accuracy inside the 25 m filter. (c) The driver held position continuously from 18:35:49 to the 18:38:50 cancellation: a dwell of 181 seconds against the 180-second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180; no_show_threshold_sec is null). POL-NS-01(c) measures that dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and expressly not from the 'arrived' event, so 18:35:49→18:38:50, i.e. 181 seconds, is the operative figure; the trace's own shortfall figure is −1.0 second, a surplus. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 18:38:50 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the dwell had elapsed (18:35:49 + 180s = 18:38:49).

The rider's two arguments are answered and rejected on their merits. First, the rider points to the platform wait timer, which started at 18:35:51 and ran 179 seconds to cancellation with no wait_timer_expired event. That does not decide limb (c): the clause fixes the measure at the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not at the platform's wait timer or the arrival tap, and the GPS clock gives 181 seconds. The two-second difference is far inside POL-NS-08(a)'s 90-second skew threshold and is resolved by POL-NS-01(c) itself, so it is not a POL-NS-09(b) contradiction. Second, the rider argues a one-second margin should not be read generously. The clause states a minimum, not a discretionary range; 181 ≥ 180 is met and there is no licence to raise the requirement.

No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces the fee. POL-NS-03 does not open: the driver's stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius, not outside it. POL-NS-04 has no foothold: the chat log (EV-CHAT-02742) contains only the driver's message, so limb (a) fails, and the rider track holds no fix inside the 100 m rider-presence radius, so limb (c) fails on admissible fixes. POL-NS-05 is not engaged: dwell_start_offset_sec is 0.0, the arrival marker coincides with the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and no false marker stands to be recomputed. POL-NS-06 finds no shortfall, and its accumulation limb (i) is not needed, the driver's dwell being one unbroken run; the MISSING traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02742-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is disclosed and named, but it carries no deciding fact and so neither caps confidence nor escalates the case.

POL-NS-07 fixes the payout at 80 percent of the net fee in force: 0.80 × 4.50 = 3.60 SGD. The anti-farming guard does not trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, below the '4 or more' threshold, and no other profile field is used. No artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08: no clock skew, no sampling gap (0.0 s maximum, 100 percent coverage), the chat log matches trip_record.chat_message_count, and the fare line of 4.50 reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. No clause produces a referral (there is no false-arrival finding under POL-NS-05(ii), no billing-integrity finding under POL-RD-09(4), and no driver-conduct item), so the referrals list is empty. Confidence is set at 0.90, below the 1.0 cap carried by the weight-1.0 artifacts that decide the case, and above the 0.70 floor, so no escalation arises. The monetary effect of 3.60 SGD is below the 8.00 SGD execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue.

To the rider: your claim that the driver cancelled almost immediately is not supported by the record, and the $4.50 cancellation fee stands; the driver is paid $3.60. To the driver: the fee is confirmed chargeable and your payout is fixed at $3.60.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. The driver was assigned at 18:29:40 and tapped 'I'm Here' at 18:35:49 (EV-TRIP-02742). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02742, weight 1.0, 100% coverage, no gaps) places the driver inside the STANDARD-class 50 m arrival radius from 18:35:49 and holds him there continuously until the 18:38:50 cancellation — a single unbroken qualifying run of 181 seconds across 19 qualifying fixes. The trip was terminated by the driver under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes the clause recognises.

POL-NS-01 — ALL FOUR LIMBS. (a) The record carries a driver 'arrived' event (18:35:49). (b) The first qualifying in-geofence fix is at that same timestamp, so the marker is not false and POL-NS-05 is not engaged (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0). (c) The free waiting period in force is 180 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec as POL-NS-01(c) and fee_schedule.resolution_rule direct. The clause measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival event and not from the platform's wait timer, and that measurement is 181 seconds — one second more than the minimum. (d) No boarding event, and the RIDER_NO_SHOW termination at 18:38:50 falls after the 180-second dwell elapsed (18:35:49 + 180 s = 18:38:49). The fee is chargeable.

THE RIDER'S ONE-SECOND ARGUMENT, ANSWERED AND REJECTED. The rider's strongest point is that the platform's own wait_timer_started event records the 180-second period beginning at 18:35:51, two seconds after the arrival tap, so the cancellation at 18:38:50 came 179 seconds later — one second short. That argument is rejected because POL-NS-01(c) expressly fixes the clock to the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not to the arrival tap or the timer event, and POL-NS-06 computes the effective dwell the same way, under POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-05. On the clock the clauses prescribe, the dwell is 181 seconds and there is no shortfall (the trace's own shortfall figure is minus one second). The rider's related point that no traffic advisory exists to allow separate intervals to be summed (EV-ADVIS-02742-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is accepted but makes no difference: the driver's dwell is a single continuous run that already meets the minimum on its own, so limb (i) of POL-NS-06 is never needed.

POL-NS-04 GIVES THE RIDER NOTHING. Limb (a) fails — the only chat message is the driver's own 'im at the pickup point' (18:36:09, EV-CHAT-02742) and the rider sent nothing — and limb (c) affirmatively fails, every one of the rider's 46 fixes sitting about 625 m from the pin, far outside the 100 m rider presence radius. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider. POL-NS-03 is not engaged: the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius, not outside it, so the 400 m wrong-entrance test never opens.

INTEGRITY AND ESCALATION. No POL-NS-08 limb fires: the arrival event matches the nearest fix to the second (limb (a)); the trace has 61 fixes and no gap over 120 s (limb (b)); the chat log's one message matches trip_record.chat_message_count of 1 (limb (c)); and the 4.50 fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50 (limb (d)). The one apparent conflict — the timer's 179 seconds against the trace's 181 — is resolved by POL-NS-01(c)'s measurement rule, so it is not a POL-NS-09(b) contradiction. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires and the case is not escalated. The decision rests on artifacts at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-02742, EV-TRIP-02742, EV-FARE-02742), so nothing discounts confidence below 0.90.

PAYOUT. POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's compensation at 80 percent of the 4.50 fee in force, that is 3.60 (derived.money.driver_compensation), the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0 against completed_trips_30d of 131, so neither limb (count of 4 or more, or rate above 0.08) is met, and compensation is payable, not withheld. On this ruling the rider's charge stands and amount_sgd carries the same 3.60 as driver_compensation_sgd, per POL-GEN-03. No clause produces a referral. The monetary effect of 3.60 does not exceed the 8.00 execution threshold, so the payment executes automatically on issue.

This ruling is addressed to both parties. The $4.50 no-show cancellation fee stands, and the driver is paid $3.60 of it as compensation. The monetary effect of $3.60 is below the execution_threshold_sgd of $8.00, so it executes automatically.

To the rider. Your claim that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is not supported by the record: the driver was assigned at 18:29:40, tapped 'I'm Here' at 18:35:49, and cancelled at 18:38:50, over nine minutes after the request. Under POL-NS-01 the fee is chargeable only if all four conditions hold, and on EV-TRIP-02742 and EV-GPS-02742 all four do. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:35:49. (b) The GPS trace places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD-class arrival radius at that same first qualifying fix, with 19 qualifying in-radius fixes. (c) The continuous in-geofence dwell, measured as POL-NS-01(c) expressly directs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix at 18:35:49 to the cancellation at 18:38:50, is 181 seconds, at or above the 180-second free waiting period read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 18:38:50 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, a code limb (d) recognises, after the 180-second dwell had elapsed at 18:38:49.

Your central argument is that the platform's wait timer (started 18:35:51) shows only 179 seconds, so the period was not served. That is rejected: POL-NS-01(c) fixes the measurement at the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not at the 'arrived' event and not at the wait timer, and the governing run is the 181-second GPS dwell (derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec; shortfall_sec -1.0). Your POL-NS-06 shortfall route therefore has no shortfall to operate on and is rejected. Your argument from the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02742-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT - impairment disclosed) is accepted but immaterial under POL-GEN-02(3): POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is indeed unavailable, yet the driver's single unbroken in-geofence run already meets the minimum on its own, so the absence changes nothing. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate you either - the chat log (EV-CHAT-02742) holds only the driver's message and none of your 46 rider fixes (622-630 m from the pin against a 100 m Standard-class radius) qualifies - so your rider-presence point, whether treated as failed or undecidable, leaves the fee decided on the driver's evidence. Your anti-farming observation is correct but does not move this case.

To the driver. POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it: POL-NS-05 is not engaged because the arrival marker at 18:35:49 coincides exactly with the first qualifying in-geofence fix (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0), and POL-NS-03 is not engaged because the qualifying fixes lie inside the 50 m radius. POL-NS-07 fixes your payout at 80 percent of the $4.50 cancellation fee in force, i.e. $3.60. The anti-farming guard does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0 (below the threshold of 4) against completed_trips_30d of 131, so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

No POL-NS-08 integrity defect arises: the fare_breakdown line of $4.50 reconciles to the net fee, the chat log matches chat_message_count, and there is no clock skew or trace gap. No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is met - confidence is above the 0.70 floor, no unresolvable artifact contradiction exists (POL-NS-01(c) resolves which clock governs), the counterparty dispute counters are 0, no_show_disputes_30d is 1, and the deciding evidence is not impaired. No clause produces a referral, so the referrals list is empty.

ledger.claim: The cancellation fee is conjunctive: POL-NS-01 makes it chargeable ONLY IF all four of its conditions hold, and the party asserting the charge carries each of them, so the rider wins by breaking any single limb. The limb that decides this case is (c) - a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least the free waiting period in force. For this trip that period is 180 seconds: trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec is 180 and platform_policy.no_show_threshold_sec is null, and under fee_schedule.resolution_rule the platform_policy figure governs because the record carries one. Limb (c) measures that dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the driver's arrival tap - which is precisely the margin on which this fee lives or dies.

On the platform's own instruments the free waiting period the rider is said to have failed to attend had not been served when the driver cancelled. The wait_timer_started event in trip_record records the 180-second free waiting period beginning at 18:35:51 ('Free waiting period of 180 s started'), and the trip was terminated at 18:38:50 - 179 seconds later - with no wait_timer_expired event anywhere in the record. POL-NS-06 makes the cancellation fee unchargeable and refunds it in full where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force under POL-NS-01(c), and that is what the platform's own wait clock shows here.

The dwell can only be the single qualifying in-geofence run, because the traffic advisory that POL-NS-06(i) requires before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed is absent from this bundle. EV-ADVIS-02742-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no payload and has admissibility weight 0.0 - I disclose that impairment expressly - so limb (i) is unavailable and no time the driver spent outside the arrival radius can be recovered into the clock. Stripping out everything limb (i) cannot supply, the effective dwell is the single 181-second run at derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run: a margin of exactly one second over the 180-second minimum on the GPS clock, and a one-second shortfall on the platform's wait-timer clock. A fee that survives only inside a one-second margin on one clock and fails on the other should not be taken from the rider.

The chargeability of this fee is measured by the driver's arrival and dwell, not by where the rider's device happened to be: POL-NS-06 refunds the fee 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. The rider track in this bundle holds 46 fixes but no qualifying fix inside the 100 m rider presence radius, and the chat_log holds no rider message, so POL-NS-04 cannot be run on this record - and that is all it means. The rider's track neither establishes the fee nor defeats it, and the dispute has to be decided on the driver's own evidence.

The driver terminated this trip at the first second the minimum dwell became available - 18:38:50 against a 180-second period running from the first qualifying fix at 18:35:49 - and the only message in the chat_log is the driver's own 'im at the pickup point' sent 20 seconds after the arrival tap and never followed up. A cancellation timed to the second of the fee's availability is the pattern POL-NS-07's anti-farming guard exists to police; the guard does not bite on this record, driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d being 0 against completed_trips_30d of 131, so nothing in POL-NS-07 requires the one-second dwell margin to be read generously - and it should not be.

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event for this trip: the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 18:35:49, some six minutes after being assigned at 18:29:40. Limb (a) of the baseline no-show test is therefore satisfied on the face of the trip record, and the rider's assertion that the driver 'cancelled almost immediately' is contradicted by the record — nine minutes and ten seconds separate the request from the cancellation.

The GPS trace places the driver inside the arrival geofence, not merely near it. The trace yields 19 qualifying in-radius fixes and the driver's qualifying run begins at the arrival timestamp 18:35:49 and ends only at the cancellation at 18:38:50. The applicable arrival radius is 50 m for the STANDARD zone class recorded on this trip, as POL-NS-02 sets it and as the arrival thresholds block restates it.

The driver held position continuously inside the geofence for 181 seconds, from the first qualifying fix at 18:35:49 to the cancellation at 18:38:50. That meets and exceeds the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec as POL-NS-01(c) directs. The trace's own shortfall figure is minus one second — a one-second surplus, not a shortfall — so the waiting-period-shortfall route under POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to operate on.

The trip was terminated by the driver at 18:38:50 under cancellation reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, and that timestamp falls after the required 180-second dwell had elapsed (18:35:49 plus 180 seconds is 18:38:49). Limb (d) holds on the record.

POL-NS-05's false-arrival route is not engaged. The arrival marker timestamp 18:35:49 coincides exactly with the first qualifying in-geofence fix from which the waiting clock runs — dwell_start_offset_sec is 0.0 — so there is no early tap and no corrected clock for POL-NS-05 to compute. The platform's own wait timer started one second later at 18:35:51 and ran to the cancellation.

POL-NS-03's wrong-entrance route is not engaged either. That clause governs only where the driver's stationary fixes lie outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; here the driver's qualifying fixes lie inside the 50 m radius itself, so the driver arrived at the pickup point and the 400 m wrong-face test never opens.

The rider cannot be exonerated under POL-NS-04. Limb (a) fails because the only message in the chat log is the driver's — 'im at the pickup point', sent 18:36:09 and read at 18:36:39 — and the rider posted nothing during the waiting window. Limb (c) affirmatively fails as well: every one of the rider's 46 recorded fixes sits between 622 m and 630 m from the pickup pin, far outside the 100 m Standard-class rider presence radius, giving zero qualifying rider fixes across the window. POL-NS-04 has no foothold.

No traffic advisory covers the pickup road. EV-ADVIS-02742-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-NS-06(i)'s accumulation of separate in-geofence intervals is unavailable and nothing can reduce the required minimum dwell. I disclose that impairment expressly under POL-GEN-02. It makes no difference to this case because the driver's dwell is a single unbroken in-geofence run that already satisfies the minimum on its own.

The fare ledger raises no integrity defect for the rider to exploit: the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line is 4.50 SGD, which is exactly the figure platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd states for this trip, so the line reconciles with the resolution rule and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. Payment status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00.

POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the 4.50 SGD cancellation fee in force, that is 3.60 SGD. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, which is not '4 or more', so neither limb of that test is met and compensation is payable rather than withheld. The outcome this trip produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, not a bare refusal to refund.
